15: # OpenCode CLI - Agent Delegation
16: 
17: How cli-opencode routes dispatches to specialized OpenCode agents via the `--agent <slug>` flag. The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes it.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: OpenCode agents are markdown files under `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`. Each file's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, system prompt, and behavioral constraints. When `opencode run --agent <slug>` is invoked, the dispatched session inherits all of that.
24: 
25: The cli-opencode skill exposes the project's full agent roster. The calling AI selects the right slug based on the task type. The agent then shapes the dispatched session: different model, different tool permissions, different system prompt.
26: 
27: ### Discovery commands
28: 
29: | Command | Purpose |
30: |---------|---------|
31: | `opencode agent list` | List all registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
32: | `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Print resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
33: | `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Print skill resolution if the agent loads one |
34: 
35: OpenCode loads `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. On OpenCode 1.19.3, user-level agents fall back from `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`), `~/.opencode/` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when the project file is missing. Which of those OpenCode 2.0.32 reads is unverified. The `debug agent` subcommand prints the merged result so the calling AI can confirm which file the dispatch will load.
36: 
37: ### Orchestration principle
38: 
39: The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes the task. The calling AI always validates and integrates the output.
40: 
41: This separation of concerns is load-bearing for the cli-opencode skill: the calling AI owns the task graph and the integration step, while the dispatched OpenCode session owns the per-task execution under the agent's tool permissions and system prompt.
42: 
43: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
48: 
49: ```text
50: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
51:   |
52:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
53:   |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
54:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
55:   |
56:   v
57: opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
58:   |
59:   |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
60:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
61:   |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
62:   |
63:   v
64: OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
65:   |
66:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
67:   |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
68:   |    step_finish) to the calling AI
69:   |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
70:   |
71:   v
72: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
73:   |
74:   |-- Parses the JSON event stream
75:   |-- Validates agent output quality
76:   |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
77:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
78: ```
79: 
80: ### Invocation pattern
81: 
82: On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:
83: 
84: ```bash
85: # OpenCode 1 only
86: opencode run \
87:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
88:   --agent <slug> \
89:   --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir /repo \
92:   "<prompt>"
93: ```
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # OpenCode 2
97: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
98:   --agent <slug> \
99:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
100:   --format json \
101:   "<prompt>"
102: ```
103: 
104: On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix, the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`. On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`). The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2. OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32. No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.
105: 
106: ### Conductor rules
107: 
108: 1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
109: 2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
110: 3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.
111: 4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
112: 5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.
113: 6. Each `opencode run` invocation is **stateless** by default. Include all necessary context in the prompt or use `--continue` / `--session <id>` for explicit continuation.
114: 7. The calling AI surfaces the JSON event stream to the operator when relevant, especially `tool_use` events.
115: 
116: ### Orchestration boundaries
117: 
118: | Concern | Owner |
119: |---------|-------|
120: | Task selection and decomposition | Calling AI |
121: | Agent slug selection | Calling AI |
122: | Prompt construction (RCAF / TIDD-EC / etc.) | Calling AI |
123: | Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |
124: | Tool permissions inside the dispatch | Agent frontmatter |
125: | System prompt and behavioral rules | Agent frontmatter |
126: | Result validation and integration | Calling AI |
127: | Memory handback extraction | Calling AI |
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 3. AGENT ROSTER
132: 
133: The repo ships these agents under `.skilled/agents/`. Three dispatch classes apply. A fix agent (or operator) MUST route each slug through its correct class, not treat the whole roster as uniformly `--agent`-dispatchable. The summary table below is followed by per-agent property tables for the most-dispatched roles.
134: 
135: | Slug | Class | Role | When to dispatch |
136: |------|-------|------|-------------------|
137: | `general` | Subagent (built-in) on 1.19.3 and 2.0.32. Top-level `--agent` REJECTED on OpenCode 1, accepted on 2.0.32. Use default (omit `--agent`) | Default implementation, complex tasks | Routine multi-step work that does not match a specialist. Never pass `--agent general`, because the default agent already runs when `--agent` is omitted |
138: | `orchestrate` | Primary, directly invokable via `--agent orchestrate` | Multi-agent coordination | Complex workflows that span several agents, or to Task-dispatch a subagent below |
139: | `context` | Subagent, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct | Read-only retrieval and codebase exploration | Search, pattern discovery, context loading. LEAF agent: no sub-dispatches, no writes |
140: | `markdown` | Subagent, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct | Template-first documentation generation | Creating READMEs, skills, guides, spec docs |
141: | `review` | Subagent, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct | Code review and PR analysis | Pre-merge reviews, quality gates. READ-ONLY |
142: | `debug` | Subagent, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct | Fresh-perspective debugging | Root cause analysis after 3+ failed debug attempts. Exclusive write access for `debug-delegation.md` |
143: | `ai-council` | Command-only (`/deep:ai-council`) or `--agent orchestrate` Task-dispatch, never direct `--agent ai-council` | Multi-strategy planning architect | Complex planning that benefits from comparing multiple solution strategies. Scoped-write: writes ONLY packet-local `ai-council/**` artifacts |
144: | `deep-research` | Command-owned by `/deep:research`, never direct `--agent deep-research` | Iterative research loop executor | Single research-cycle dispatches. State externalized to packet-local JSONL + strategy.md |
145: | `deep-review` | Command-owned by `/deep:review`, never direct `--agent deep-review` | Iterative code review loop executor | Single review-cycle dispatches. P0/P1/P2 findings, severity-weighted convergence |
146: | `prompt-improver` | Command-owned by `/prompt`, never direct `--agent prompt-improver` | Dispatch-ready prompt package generation | Deep-path prompt escalation per the cli-* prompt-quality-card Tier 3 trigger |
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ### @context: Read-Only Codebase Explorer
151: 
152: | Property | Value |
153: |----------|-------|
154: | **Role** | Read-only codebase exploration and pattern discovery |
155: | **Sandbox** | Read-only (no writes, no sub-dispatches) |
156: | **Modifies files** | Never |
157: | **LEAF constraint** | YES: single iteration, no nested dispatches |
158: 
159: **Best for:** File discovery, pattern analysis, dependency tracing, architecture mapping, gathering context before implementation.
160: 
161: **Delegate when:** The calling AI needs structured codebase exploration with read-only safety guarantees.
162: 
163: ---
164: 
165: ### @debug: Fresh-Perspective Debugger
166: 
167: | Property | Value |
168: |----------|-------|
169: | **Role** | Systematic debugging with fresh context |
170: | **Sandbox** | Workspace-write (bug fixes only) |
171: | **Modifies files** | Yes (bug fixes plus exclusive write access for `debug-delegation.md`) |
172: | **LEAF constraint** | No |
173: 
174: **Best for:** Bugs that resist initial debugging (3+ failed attempts), root cause analysis, reproducing elusive errors.
175: 
176: **Delegate when:** The calling AI's own debug attempts have failed. The fresh perspective avoids inheriting wrong assumptions from the parent conversation.
177: 
178: **Methodology:** Observe -> Analyze -> Hypothesize -> Fix.
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ### @review: Code Quality Guardian
183: 
184: | Property | Value |
185: |----------|-------|
186: | **Role** | Code review, severity scoring, security audits |
187: | **Sandbox** | Read-only |
188: | **Modifies files** | Never |
189: | **LEAF constraint** | No |
190: 
191: **Best for:** Pre-merge reviews, security audits, P0 / P1 / P2 severity classification.
192: 
193: **Delegate when:** The calling AI wants a second perspective on code quality, or needs to validate its own implementation from a different model's viewpoint.
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: 
198: ### @ai-council: Multi-Strategy Planning Architect
199: 
200: | Property | Value |
201: |----------|-------|
202: | **Role** | Multi-strategy planning across diverse thinking lenses |
203: | **Sandbox** | Scoped-write |
204: | **Modifies files** | Yes, but ONLY packet-local `ai-council/**` artifacts (never any other path) |
205: | **LEAF constraint** | SCOPED-WRITE (writes and edits confined to `ai-council/**`, never touching code or other spec docs) |
206: 
207: **Best for:** Architecture decisions, complex planning that benefits from comparing 3+ solution strategies.
208: 
209: **Command-only (as of `mode: subagent`).** On OpenCode 1, direct `opencode run --agent ai-council` is not reachable: `ai-council.md` is `mode: subagent`, not directly selectable as a top-level session agent. OpenCode 2.0.32 does select a subagent slug directly, so there the routing rule, not the binary, keeps `ai-council` behind its command. Dispatch via `/deep:ai-council` for a full session, or via `opencode run --agent orchestrate "..."` and let `orchestrate`'s own routing Task-dispatch to `@ai-council` for a single planning pass (never `--agent general`, which OpenCode 1 rejects at the top level).
210: 
211: **Delegate when:** The calling AI needs a fundamentally different planning approach or wants to compare strategies before committing to one.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ### @deep-research and @deep-review: Loop Executors
216: 
217: These two agents are dispatched only by their parent commands. The calling AI does NOT route to them directly.
218: 
219: | Slug | Parent command | Loop role |
220: |------|----------------|-----------|
221: | `deep-research` | `/deep:research` | Single research iteration with externalized JSONL + strategy.md state |
222: | `deep-review` | `/deep:review` | Single review iteration with P0/P1/P2 findings and severity-weighted convergence |
223: 
224: Both are LEAF agents. Each iteration is fresh-context. The parent command owns convergence detection and state continuity.
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: ## 4. AGENT ROUTING MATRIX
229: 
230: Pick the agent that matches the task type. Default to omitting `--agent` (the `general` default) when no specialist fits.
231: 
232: | Task type | Agent | Invocation pattern |
233: |-----------|-------|---------------------|
234: | Codebase exploration | `context` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the context subagent: map the dependency graph for src/"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the context subagent: map the dependency graph for src/"` |
235: | Multi-agent coordination | `orchestrate` | On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Coordinate review and testing of auth module"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Coordinate review and testing of auth module"` |
236: | Documentation generation | `markdown` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the markdown subagent: generate a README for the cli-opencode skill"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the markdown subagent: generate a README for the cli-opencode skill"` |
237: | Code review | `review` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the review subagent: review @src/auth.ts for security issues"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the review subagent: review @src/auth.ts for security issues"`. Or use the `As @review:` prompt-prefix pattern in §5, with no `--agent` flag at all |
238: | Root cause debugging | `debug` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the debug subagent: debug this error: <error>"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the debug subagent: debug this error: <error>"` |
239: | Iterative research loop | `deep-research` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:research` (or `/deep:research:auto`). Direct `opencode run --agent deep-research` is forbidden. The parent command owns iteration state, JSONL, and convergence. |
240: | Iterative code review loop | `deep-review` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:review` (or `/deep:review:auto`). Direct `opencode run --agent deep-review` is forbidden. The parent command owns iteration state and severity-weighted convergence. |
241: | Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:ai-council` for a full session, or, on OpenCode 1, `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Dispatch @ai-council: plan the authentication redesign — compare three strategies. Spec folder: <pre-bound packet>."` (on OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Dispatch @ai-council: plan the authentication redesign — compare three strategies. Spec folder: <pre-bound packet>."`) and let orchestrate's routing Task-dispatch `@ai-council`, scoped-write to that packet's `ai-council/**`. Direct `opencode run --agent ai-council` is forbidden as of `mode: subagent`. |
242: | Default / unspecified | (none, omit `--agent`) | On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "<prompt>"`. Never pass `--agent general`, because OpenCode 1 rejects it at the top level |
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## 5. THE `As @<agent>` PROMPT-TIME PATTERN
247: 
248: Mirroring the sibling cli-* skills, cli-opencode supports an inline routing pattern where the calling AI prefixes the prompt with `As @<agent>:` instead of using the `--agent` flag. This is useful when the calling AI dispatches a single `opencode run` and shifts agent behavior mid-session.
249: 
250: ```bash
251: # OpenCode 1 only
252: opencode run \
253:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
254:   --variant max \
255:   --format json \
256:   --dir /repo \
257:   "As @review: Inspect @src/auth.ts for security issues. Surface any P0 / P1 findings with file:line citations."
258: ```
259: 
260: ```bash
261: # OpenCode 2
262: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
263:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
264:   --format json \
265:   "As @review: Inspect @src/auth.ts for security issues. Surface any P0 / P1 findings with file:line citations."
266: ```
267: 
268: On OpenCode 1, the dispatched session parses the `As @review:` prefix and loads the review agent's frontmatter from `.opencode/agents/review.md`. The remaining prompt is passed to that agent. OpenCode 2.0.32 does not: an `As @review:` body runs under the default agent there. The routing rule above still sends review work through `--agent orchestrate`, whose subagent routing is untested on OpenCode 2.0.32.
269: 
270: ### When to prefer `--agent` vs `As @<agent>:`
271: 
272: | Pattern | When |
273: |---------|------|
274: | `--agent <slug>` | Routine routing: the calling AI knows the right agent up front |
275: | `As @<agent>:` | The calling AI wants the agent slug to be visible in the prompt for debugging or telemetry |
276: 
277: ---
278: 
279: ## 6. MULTI-AGENT WORKFLOWS
280: 
281: cli-opencode dispatches that touch multiple agents follow this pattern:
282: 
283: 1. Use `--agent orchestrate` for the entry-point dispatch.
284: 2. The orchestrator spawns sub-agents through OpenCode's native Task tool (NOT through nested `opencode run` invocations, which break the orchestration tree).
285: 3. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream to surface tool calls and partial messages.
286: 
287: Example:
288: 
289: ```bash
290: # OpenCode 1 only
291: opencode run \
292:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
293:   --agent orchestrate \
294:   --variant max \
295:   --format json \
296:   --dir /repo \
297:   "Coordinate a code review for the approved spec folder. Dispatch @review for the code. Aggregate findings."
298: ```
299: 
300: ```bash
301: # OpenCode 2
302: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
303:   --agent orchestrate \
304:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
305:   --format json \
306:   "Coordinate a code review for the approved spec folder. Dispatch @review for the code. Aggregate findings."
307: ```
308: 
309: ### Avoiding double orchestration
310: 
311: If the calling AI is already decomposing tasks, delegate directly to leaf agents instead of routing through `@orchestrate`. Stacking orchestrators wastes a turn and obscures the task graph.
312: 
313: | Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Correct approach |
314: |--------------|--------------|------------------|
315: | Calling AI -> `@orchestrate` -> single leaf agent | Orchestrator overhead with no coordination benefit | Delegate directly to the leaf agent |
316: | Calling AI -> `@orchestrate` -> `@orchestrate` -> leaf | Two orchestration layers with the same task graph | Pick one orchestrator, decompose once |
317: 
318: ---
319: 
320: ## 7. LEAF-AGENT CONSTRAINTS
321: 
322: Some agents are LEAF agents by design. Most MUST NOT dispatch sub-agents, use the Task tool, or write files (read-only). `ai-council` is the one LEAF exception, confined to a scoped-write subtree instead of full read-only. The cli-opencode skill MUST honor these constraints:
323: 
324: | Agent | Constraint |
325: |-------|-----------|
326: | `context` | LEAF: no sub-dispatches, no writes. All results returned to the caller |
327: | `deep-research` | LEAF: single iteration, externalized state, no nested dispatches |
328: | `deep-review` | LEAF: single iteration, externalized state, no nested dispatches |
329: | `ai-council` | LEAF, no sub-dispatches, but SCOPED-WRITE (not read-only): writes and edits confined to the pre-bound packet's `ai-council/**` subtree only |
330: 
331: The calling AI must NOT request a write outside `ai-council/**` or a sub-dispatch from a LEAF agent. If the prompt would require either, route to `orchestrate` instead (never `general`, which OpenCode 1 rejects at the top level).
332: 
333: ---
334: 
335: ## 8. WORKED EXAMPLES
336: 
337: Two end-to-end examples covering the most common dispatch patterns.
338: 
339: ### Example 1: Code review via `@review`
340: 
341: The calling AI wants a security-focused review of a single file. No `--agent` flag: `review` is a subagent, not directly invokable at the top level. The `As @review:` prompt prefix carries the role instead (or route via `--agent orchestrate` and ask it to dispatch the review subagent).
342: 
343: ```bash
344: # OpenCode 1 only
345: opencode run \
346:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
347:   --variant max \
348:   --format json \
349:   --dir /path/to/repo \
350:   "As @review: audit @src/auth/handler.ts for OWASP Top 10 issues. Surface findings as P0 / P1 / P2 with file:line citations. READ-ONLY — do not propose fixes."
351: ```
352: 
353: ```bash
354: # OpenCode 2
355: cd /path/to/repo && opencode run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
357:   --format json \
358:   "As @review: audit @src/auth/handler.ts for OWASP Top 10 issues. Surface findings as P0 / P1 / P2 with file:line citations. READ-ONLY — do not propose fixes."
359: ```
360: 
361: **Expected handback:** JSON event stream with `tool_use` events for file reads, plus a final assistant message containing the structured P0 / P1 / P2 list.
362: 
363: **Calling AI follow-up:** Validate that every cited line resolves in the source file. Re-dispatch with refined scope if a finding lacks evidence.
364: 
365: ---
366: 
367: 
368: ### Example 2: Root cause debugging via `@debug`
369: 
370: The calling AI's first 3 debug attempts failed. Escalate to a fresh-context dispatch. No `--agent` flag: `debug` is a subagent, not directly invokable at the top level. The `As @debug:` prompt prefix carries the role instead (or route via `--agent orchestrate` and ask it to dispatch the debug subagent).
371: 
372: ```bash
373: # OpenCode 1 only
374: opencode run \
375:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
376:   --variant max \
377:   --format json \
378:   --dir /path/to/repo \
379:   "As @debug: Login returns 401 despite valid credentials. Error at @src/auth/handler.ts:45. Prior attempts: verified token expiry, checked DB connection, confirmed env vars. Run the Observe -> Analyze -> Hypothesize -> Fix methodology. Write findings to debug-delegation.md."
380: ```
381: 
382: ```bash
383: # OpenCode 2
384: cd /path/to/repo && opencode run --standalone \
385:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
386:   --format json \
387:   "As @debug: Login returns 401 despite valid credentials. Error at @src/auth/handler.ts:45. Prior attempts: verified token expiry, checked DB connection, confirmed env vars. Run the Observe -> Analyze -> Hypothesize -> Fix methodology. Write findings to debug-delegation.md."
388: ```
389: 
390: **Expected handback:** JSON event stream including a write to `debug-delegation.md` and a final summary with root cause + applied fix (or refusal with rationale).
391: 
392: **Calling AI follow-up:** Read `debug-delegation.md`. If a fix was applied, run the project's test suite. If `@debug` declined to fix, surface the rationale to the operator.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 9. FAILURE MODES AND OUTPUT HANDLING
397: 
398: ### Capturing output
399: 
400: ```bash
401: # Capture JSON event stream to file (no --agent; subagent role carried in the prompt)
402: # OpenCode 1 only
403: opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo \
404:   "As @review: review @src/auth.ts" > /tmp/review-events.jsonl
405: 
406: # OpenCode 2
407: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json \
408:   "As @review: review @src/auth.ts" > /tmp/review-events.jsonl
409: 
410: # Capture stdout to a variable (no --agent; subagent role carried in the prompt)
411: # OpenCode 1 only
412: RESULT=$(opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo \
413:   "As @context: list exported symbols in src/")
414: 
415: # OpenCode 2
416: RESULT=$(cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json \
417:   "As @context: list exported symbols in src/")
418: 
419: # Check exit status
420: if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
421:   echo "Success"
422: else
423:   echo "opencode run failed" >&2
424: fi
425: ```
426: 
427: ### Parsing structured output
428: 
429: `--format json` emits newline-delimited JSON events. Each event has at minimum `type`, `timestamp`, `sessionID`, and `part`. The calling AI parses incrementally:
430: 
431: ```bash
432: jq -r 'select(.type == "tool_use") | .part.tool' /tmp/review-events.jsonl
433: jq -r 'select(.type == "text") | .part.text' /tmp/review-events.jsonl
434: ```
435: 
436: ### Failure modes
437: 
438: | Symptom | Likely cause | Recovery |
439: |---------|--------------|----------|
440: | `unknown agent <slug>` | Slug not present in `.opencode/agents/` or user-level fallback | Run `opencode agent list` to enumerate, fix the slug, retry |
441: | Agent loaded but writes refused | LEAF agent constraint or read-only sandbox | Re-route to `general` / `orchestrate` for write operations |
442: | Session never finishes | Tool call hung or infinite loop | Inspect `~/.opencode/state/<sessionID>/messages.jsonl`, abort the session, retry with refined scope |
443: | Empty output stream | `--format default` with non-TTY parent | Pass `--format json` and parse the event stream |
444: | Plugin load crash | Misconfigured plugin in agent context | On OpenCode 1, rerun with `--pure` to bypass plugins, then root-cause the plugin. OpenCode 2 `run` has no `--pure` (see `./install-and-versions.md`) |
445: | `provider/model not found` | Model not configured for the agent's chosen provider | Run `opencode providers` to enumerate, then `auth login <provider>` |
446: | Self-invocation refused | cli-opencode detected an in-OpenCode runtime | Use a sibling cli-* skill or restate the request with parallel-session keywords (see ADR-001) |
447: | Low-quality agent output | Wrong agent for the task or under-specified prompt | Re-route per the routing matrix, refine the prompt with more context |
448: 
449: ### Recovery patterns
450: 
451: When a dispatch produces low-quality output, the calling AI has three escalation paths:
452: 
453: 1. **Refine the prompt.** Add file anchors, success criteria, or "do not change" guardrails. Re-dispatch with the same agent.
454: 2. **Re-route to a different agent.** If `@orchestrate` produced thin docs, escalate with `--variant max` on OpenCode 1 (on OpenCode 2, the `#max` suffix on `-m`) for multi-pass refinement.
455: 3. **Decompose the task.** Break the dispatch into smaller sub-tasks with explicit handoffs between agents. Each sub-task gets its own validation step.
456: 
457: The conductor (calling AI) decides which path. The agent has no visibility into the parent task graph.
458: 
459: ---
460: 
461: ## 10. RELATED RESOURCES
462:

464: - `./integration-patterns.md` - Three use cases that drive agent selection
465: - `./opencode-tools.md` - Why agent dispatch matters relative to sibling cli-* skills
466: - `../assets/prompt-templates.md` - Copy-paste templates per agent
467: - `../ROUTER.md` - Smart router pseudocode

14: 
15: # OpenCode CLI - Agent Delegation
16: 
17: How cli-opencode routes dispatches to specialized OpenCode agents via the `--agent <slug>` flag. The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes it.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: OpenCode agents are markdown files under `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`. Each file's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, system prompt, and behavioral constraints. When `opencode run --agent <slug>` is invoked, the dispatched session inherits all of that.
24: 
25: The cli-opencode skill exposes the project's full agent roster. The calling AI selects the right slug based on the task type. The agent then shapes the dispatched session: different model, different tool permissions, different system prompt.
26: 
27: ### Discovery commands
28: 
29: | Command | Purpose |
30: |---------|---------|
31: | `opencode agent list` | List all registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
32: | `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Print resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
33: | `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Print skill resolution if the agent loads one |
34: 
35: OpenCode loads `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. On OpenCode 1.19.3, user-level agents fall back from `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`), `~/.opencode/` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when the project file is missing. Which of those OpenCode 2.0.32 reads is unverified. The `debug agent` subcommand prints the merged result so the calling AI can confirm which file the dispatch will load.
36: 
37: ### Orchestration principle
38: 
39: The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes the task. The calling AI always validates and integrates the output.
40: 
41: This separation of concerns is load-bearing for the cli-opencode skill: the calling AI owns the task graph and the integration step, while the dispatched OpenCode session owns the per-task execution under the agent's tool permissions and system prompt.
42: 
43: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
48: 
49: ```text
50: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
51:   |
52:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
53:   |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
54:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
55:   |
56:   v
57: opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
58:   |
59:   |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
60:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
61:   |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
62:   |
63:   v
64: OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
65:   |
66:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
67:   |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
68:   |    step_finish) to the calling AI
69:   |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
70:   |
71:   v
72: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
73:   |
74:   |-- Parses the JSON event stream
75:   |-- Validates agent output quality
76:   |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
77:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
78: ```
79: 
80: ### Invocation pattern
81: 
82: On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:
83: 
84: ```bash
85: # OpenCode 1 only
86: opencode run \
87:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
88:   --agent <slug> \
89:   --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir /repo \
92:   "<prompt>"
93: ```
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # OpenCode 2
97: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
98:   --agent <slug> \
99:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
100:   --format json \
101:   "<prompt>"
102: ```
103: 
104: On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix, the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`. On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`). The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2. OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32. No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.
105: 
106: ### Conductor rules
107: 
108: 1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
109: 2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
110: 3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.

246: ## 5. THE `As @<agent>` PROMPT-TIME PATTERN
247: 
248: Mirroring the sibling cli-* skills, cli-opencode supports an inline routing pattern where the calling AI prefixes the prompt with `As @<agent>:` instead of using the `--agent` flag. This is useful when the calling AI dispatches a single `opencode run` and shifts agent behavior mid-session.
249: 
250: ```bash
251: # OpenCode 1 only
252: opencode run \
253:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
254:   --variant max \
255:   --format json \
256:   --dir /repo \
257:   "As @review: Inspect @src/auth.ts for security issues. Surface any P0 / P1 findings with file:line citations."
258: ```
259: 
260: ```bash
261: # OpenCode 2
262: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
263:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
264:   --format json \
265:   "As @review: Inspect @src/auth.ts for security issues. Surface any P0 / P1 findings with file:line citations."
266: ```
267: 
268: On OpenCode 1, the dispatched session parses the `As @review:` prefix and loads the review agent's frontmatter from `.opencode/agents/review.md`. The remaining prompt is passed to that agent. OpenCode 2.0.32 does not: an `As @review:` body runs under the default agent there. The routing rule above still sends review work through `--agent orchestrate`, whose subagent routing is untested on OpenCode 2.0.32.

273: |---------|------|
274: | `--agent <slug>` | Routine routing: the calling AI knows the right agent up front |
275: | `As @<agent>:` | The calling AI wants the agent slug to be visible in the prompt for debugging or telemetry |

279: ## 6. MULTI-AGENT WORKFLOWS
280: 
281: cli-opencode dispatches that touch multiple agents follow this pattern:
282: 
283: 1. Use `--agent orchestrate` for the entry-point dispatch.
284: 2. The orchestrator spawns sub-agents through OpenCode's native Task tool (NOT through nested `opencode run` invocations, which break the orchestration tree).
285: 3. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream to surface tool calls and partial messages.
286: 
287: Example:
288: 
289: ```bash
290: # OpenCode 1 only
291: opencode run \
292:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
293:   --agent orchestrate \
294:   --variant max \
295:   --format json \
296:   --dir /repo \
297:   "Coordinate a code review for the approved spec folder. Dispatch @review for the code. Aggregate findings."
298: ```
299: 
300: ```bash
301: # OpenCode 2
302: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
303:   --agent orchestrate \
304:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
305:   --format json \
306:   "Coordinate a code review for the approved spec folder. Dispatch @review for the code. Aggregate findings."
307: ```
308: 
309: ### Avoiding double orchestration
310: 
311: If the calling AI is already decomposing tasks, delegate directly to leaf agents instead of routing through `@orchestrate`. Stacking orchestrators wastes a turn and obscures the task graph.
312: 
313: | Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Correct approach |
314: |--------------|--------------|------------------|
315: | Calling AI -> `@orchestrate` -> single leaf agent | Orchestrator overhead with no coordination benefit | Delegate directly to the leaf agent |
316: | Calling AI -> `@orchestrate` -> `@orchestrate` -> leaf | Two orchestration layers with the same task graph | Pick one orchestrator, decompose once |

320: ## 7. LEAF-AGENT CONSTRAINTS
321: 
322: Some agents are LEAF agents by design. Most MUST NOT dispatch sub-agents, use the Task tool, or write files (read-only). `ai-council` is the one LEAF exception, confined to a scoped-write subtree instead of full read-only. The cli-opencode skill MUST honor these constraints:
323: 
324: | Agent | Constraint |
325: |-------|-----------|
326: | `context` | LEAF: no sub-dispatches, no writes. All results returned to the caller |
327: | `deep-research` | LEAF: single iteration, externalized state, no nested dispatches |
328: | `deep-review` | LEAF: single iteration, externalized state, no nested dispatches |
329: | `ai-council` | LEAF, no sub-dispatches, but SCOPED-WRITE (not read-only): writes and edits confined to the pre-bound packet's `ai-council/**` subtree only |
330: 
331: The calling AI must NOT request a write outside `ai-council/**` or a sub-dispatch from a LEAF agent. If the prompt would require either, route to `orchestrate` instead (never `general`, which OpenCode 1 rejects at the top level).

396: ## 9. FAILURE MODES AND OUTPUT HANDLING
397: 
398: ### Capturing output
399: 
400: ```bash
401: # Capture JSON event stream to file (no --agent; subagent role carried in the prompt)
402: # OpenCode 1 only
403: opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo \
404:   "As @review: review @src/auth.ts" > /tmp/review-events.jsonl
405: 
406: # OpenCode 2
407: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json \
408:   "As @review: review @src/auth.ts" > /tmp/review-events.jsonl
409: 
410: # Capture stdout to a variable (no --agent; subagent role carried in the prompt)
411: # OpenCode 1 only
412: RESULT=$(opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo \
413:   "As @context: list exported symbols in src/")
414: 
415: # OpenCode 2
416: RESULT=$(cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json \
417:   "As @context: list exported symbols in src/")
418: 
419: # Check exit status
420: if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
421:   echo "Success"
422: else
423:   echo "opencode run failed" >&2
424: fi
425: ```
426: 
427: ### Parsing structured output
428: 
429: `--format json` emits newline-delimited JSON events. Each event has at minimum `type`, `timestamp`, `sessionID`, and `part`. The calling AI parses incrementally:
430: 
431: ```bash
432: jq -r 'select(.type == "tool_use") | .part.tool' /tmp/review-events.jsonl
433: jq -r 'select(.type == "text") | .part.text' /tmp/review-events.jsonl
434: ```
435: 
436: ### Failure modes
437: 
438: | Symptom | Likely cause | Recovery |
439: |---------|--------------|----------|
440: | `unknown agent <slug>` | Slug not present in `.opencode/agents/` or user-level fallback | Run `opencode agent list` to enumerate, fix the slug, retry |
441: | Agent loaded but writes refused | LEAF agent constraint or read-only sandbox | Re-route to `general` / `orchestrate` for write operations |
442: | Session never finishes | Tool call hung or infinite loop | Inspect `~/.opencode/state/<sessionID>/messages.jsonl`, abort the session, retry with refined scope |
443: | Empty output stream | `--format default` with non-TTY parent | Pass `--format json` and parse the event stream |
444: | Plugin load crash | Misconfigured plugin in agent context | On OpenCode 1, rerun with `--pure` to bypass plugins, then root-cause the plugin. OpenCode 2 `run` has no `--pure` (see `./install-and-versions.md`) |
445: | `provider/model not found` | Model not configured for the agent's chosen provider | Run `opencode providers` to enumerate, then `auth login <provider>` |
446: | Self-invocation refused | cli-opencode detected an in-OpenCode runtime | Use a sibling cli-* skill or restate the request with parallel-session keywords (see ADR-001) |
447: | Low-quality agent output | Wrong agent for the task or under-specified prompt | Re-route per the routing matrix, refine the prompt with more context |
448: 
449: ### Recovery patterns
450: 
451: When a dispatch produces low-quality output, the calling AI has three escalation paths:
452: 
453: 1. **Refine the prompt.** Add file anchors, success criteria, or "do not change" guardrails. Re-dispatch with the same agent.
454: 2. **Re-route to a different agent.** If `@orchestrate` produced thin docs, escalate with `--variant max` on OpenCode 1 (on OpenCode 2, the `#max` suffix on `-m`) for multi-pass refinement.
455: 3. **Decompose the task.** Break the dispatch into smaller sub-tasks with explicit handoffs between agents. Each sub-task gets its own validation step.
456: 
457: The conductor (calling AI) decides which path. The agent has no visibility into the parent task graph.

Executing a registered command non-interactively requires `--command <family>/<name>` with the args as the message (they become `$ARGUMENTS`). Registry names are slash-namespaced (`speckit/search` for `/speckit:search`). A wrong name fails with the full registry list. Behavior probes of slash commands MUST use `--command`. The raw-text form only measures the model freestyling without the contract. Consequences: (a) any behavior/adherence probe of a slash command MUST use `--command`, and the raw-text form is only valid as a labeled negative control. (b) Inside `` !`…` `` template injections `$ARGUMENTS` expands like `"$@"`, one word per argument, so renderer scripts must join argv themselves. On OpenCode 2 there is no `run` flag for a registered command: the command runs through the server API (`POST /api/session/{id}/command`).
150: 
151: ### cli-opencode default invocation shape
152: 
153: The skill builds every dispatch from a base shape and overlays use-case-specific flags. The recommended OpenCode 2 base shape comes first; the OpenCode 1 fallback follows.
154: 
155: ```bash
156: # OpenCode 2 (recommended)
157: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
158:   --agent <agent-slug> \
159:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
160:   --format json \
161:   "<prompt>"
162: ```
163: 
164: ```bash
165: # OpenCode 1 only (fallback)
166: opencode run \
167:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
168:   --agent <agent-slug> \
169:   --variant max \
170:   --format json \
171:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
172:   "<prompt>"
173: ```
174: 
175: On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into the `cd`, and the `--variant max` effort becomes the `#max` suffix on `-m`. On OpenCode 1 the working directory rides in `--dir` and effort stays in `--variant`. A child dispatch adds `--standalone`. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions; a v2 reader confirms that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `llmgateway/` prefix first.
176: 
177: | Flag | Default | Reason |
178: |------|---------|--------|
179: | `-m`, `--model` (OpenCode 2, recommended) | `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max` | The DevPass LLM Gateway fronts the latency-optimized flash model, with max-tier effort as the `#max` suffix on the model id. The operator may override it (e.g. `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` on the OpenCode 1 fallback, or any live OpenAI GPT-6 slug: `openai/gpt-6-sol`, `openai/gpt-6-sol-fast`, `openai/gpt-6-luna`, `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, `openai/gpt-6.1-terra-fast`) |
180: | `--model`, `--variant max` (OpenCode 1, fallback) | `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, variant max | Same default model. The default is max-tier-pinned by policy, so a lower requested effort is upgraded automatically. On OpenCode 2 the effort rides on `-m` as `#max` |
181: | `--agent` | per use case | Required for use case 1 / 3, optional for use case 2 |
182: | `--format json` | json | Structured event stream is what external runtimes parse |
183: | `--dir` (OpenCode 1, fallback) | repo root | Pin the working directory to avoid CWD ambiguity. On OpenCode 2 there is no `--dir`, so start the dispatch in the repo root: `cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run ...` |
184: 
185: ### Stdin handling: `</dev/null` is required for non-interactive dispatch
186: 
187: > **On OpenCode 1 (v1.14.39), opencode reads stdin at startup before session creation.** If you redirect stdout/stderr to files in automation (`> stdout.log 2> stderr.log`), opencode hangs at 0% CPU after the `+60s snapshot prune cleanup` log line because stdin remains attached to the parent terminal and never receives EOF. The hang is observed on OpenCode 1, and whether OpenCode 2 (the recommended target) shares it is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32, so the redirect stays on both versions.
188: 
189: ALWAYS append `</dev/null` AFTER the prompt argument and BEFORE the stdout/stderr redirects:
190: 
191: ```bash
192: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" </dev/null > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
193: #                                  ^^^^^^^^^^
194: #                                  redirects stdin from /dev/null → immediate EOF
195: ```
196: 
197: Foreground `| tail` accidentally works because the upstream pipe stage provides closed stdin, but `> file 2> file` does not. See `references/integration-patterns.md` §6 for the full failure-mode + fix matrix and `../CHANGELOG-2026-05-08-tool-name-regex-fix.md` §Fix 4 for the discovery context.
198: 
199: ### Sessions, share URLs, and ports
200: 
201: On OpenCode 2 `run` there is no `--share` flag at all. On the OpenCode 1 fallback (1.19.3), `--share` is a hidden and deprecated option: passing it prints `!  Session sharing has been discontinued` and the run carries on, but nothing is published and no URL is printed. No dispatch should pass `--share`.
202: 
203: On OpenCode 2, `--port` is absent on `run` (see [install-and-versions.md](./install-and-versions.md)). On the OpenCode 1 fallback, `--port` only matters when the dispatch needs to bind a known port (e.g. for a parallel detached session that another tool will attach to); the default random port is correct for one-shot dispatches.
204: 
205: `--continue` and `--session <id>` reuse prior session state. `--fork` branches an existing session into a new one. cli-opencode uses session continuation in memory handback flows where the calling AI wants to thread context across multiple delegations.
206: 
207: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (smart fallback)
208: 
209: Before the first dispatch in a session, run a one-shot auth pre-flight so a missing default doesn't fail mid-dispatch. OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) is the recommended path: list with `opencode models --standalone` and filter for the `<provider-id>/` prefix, because v2 `models` takes no provider argument. On the OpenCode 1 fallback, `opencode models <provider-id>` exits 0 when the provider is configured and 1 when it is not; OpenCode 2 rejects that form with `Unexpected positional argument`. `--standalone` runs a private server instead of asking the shared background service. Do not grep `opencode providers list` for ids: it prints display names such as `OpenCode Go` and `DevPass (LLM Gateway)`. Cache the result for the session and re-run it only on auth failure.
210: 
211: Run the block for the version you are about to dispatch. Side by side, OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode1`, so replace `opencode` with `opencode1` in the OpenCode 1 block there.
212: 
213: ```bash
214: # OpenCode 2 pre-flight: `models` takes no provider argument, so list once on a private server and filter per provider
215: V2_MODELS=$(opencode models --standalone 2>/dev/null)
216: printf '%s\n' "$V2_MODELS" | grep '^llmgateway/'  >/dev/null && LLMGATEWAY_OK=1 || LLMGATEWAY_OK=0    # LLM Gateway (DevPass); the default route
217: printf '%s\n' "$V2_MODELS" | grep '^opencode-go/' >/dev/null && OPENCODE_GO_OK=1 || OPENCODE_GO_OK=0  # OpenCode Go gateway (2.0.32 lists none here unless logged in separately)
218: DEFAULT_OK=$LLMGATEWAY_OK                                                                             # OpenCode 2 default is on LLM Gateway
219: MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK=0; MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK=0                                                               # 2.0.32 lists no minimax provider
220: echo "default=$DEFAULT_OK opencode_go=$OPENCODE_GO_OK minimax_token=$MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK minimax_direct=$MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK llmgateway=$LLMGATEWAY_OK"
221: ```
222: 
223: ```bash
224: # OpenCode 1 pre-flight (fallback): one check per provider id, once per session
225: opencode models opencode-go         >/dev/null 2>&1 && OPENCODE_GO_OK=1  || OPENCODE_GO_OK=0   # OpenCode 1: OpenCode Go gateway (selectable; fronts DeepSeek V4 Flash, Qwen, GLM)
226: opencode models minimax-coding-plan >/dev/null 2>&1 && MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK=1  || MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK=0   # OpenCode 1: MiniMax Token Plan (default MiniMax path)
227: opencode models minimax             >/dev/null 2>&1 && MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK=1 || MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK=0  # OpenCode 1: MiniMax Direct API (pay-per-token)
228: opencode models llmgateway          >/dev/null 2>&1 && LLMGATEWAY_OK=1    || LLMGATEWAY_OK=0      # OpenCode 1: LLM Gateway (DevPass); the default route
229: DEFAULT_OK=$LLMGATEWAY_OK                                                                            # OpenCode 1 default is on LLM Gateway
230: echo "default=$DEFAULT_OK opencode_go=$OPENCODE_GO_OK minimax_token=$MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK minimax_direct=$MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK llmgateway=$LLMGATEWAY_OK"
231: ```
232: 
233: | State | DEFAULT_OK | Action |
234: |-------|----------------|--------|
235: | Default available | 1 | Proceed with `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max` on OpenCode 2 (confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `llmgateway/` prefix first), or `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max` on the OpenCode 1 fallback |
236: | Default missing | 0 | **ASK user** before substituting (offer A: openai/gpt-6-sol, B: set up the default provider — `llmgateway` on both versions — and retry, C: name a different model). Do not dispatch until configured |
237: 
238: **MiniMax routing** (default = Token Plan, Direct API is the pay-per-token alternative):
239: 
240: | State | Condition | Action |
241: |-------|-----------|--------|
242: | MiniMax requested (default) | `MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK=1` | Proceed with `--model minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3` and **omit `--agent`** (rejected on opencode 1.15.13) |
243: | Token Plan not configured | `MINIMAX_TOKEN_OK=0` | **ASK user** to run `opencode auth login` → MiniMax Token Plan. Never substitute silently |
244: | Direct API explicitly requested | `MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK=1` | Proceed with `--model minimax/MiniMax-M3` (pay-per-token, confirm the live id via `opencode models minimax` on OpenCode 1) |
245: | Direct API requested, not configured | `MINIMAX_DIRECT_OK=0` | **ASK user** to configure the `minimax` provider (`MINIMAX_API_KEY`). Do not substitute silently |
246: 
247: **Login / setup command shapes** (the AI surfaces these to the user, who runs them in their own terminal):
248: 
249: ```bash
250: # OpenCode 2 default (recommended) — LLM Gateway (DevPass). Interactive: pick "DevPass (LLM Gateway)".
251: opencode providers login llmgateway
252: 
253: # OpenCode 1 default (fallback) — LLM Gateway (DevPass). Interactive: pick "DevPass (LLM Gateway)".
254: opencode providers login llmgateway
255: 
256: # OpenCode 1 selectable (fallback) — OpenCode Go gateway
257: opencode providers login opencode-go
258: 
259: # MiniMax Token Plan — DEFAULT MiniMax path (subscription). Interactive: pick "MiniMax Token Plan (minimax.io)".
260: opencode auth login          # → provider minimax-coding-plan; Anthropic-compatible https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1 (China: api.minimaxi.com)
261: 
262: # MiniMax Direct API — pay-per-token alternative (needs MINIMAX_API_KEY; platform endpoint https://api.minimax.io/v1)
263: opencode providers login minimax
264: 
265: # Z.AI GLM Coding Plan — GLM coding subscription. Interactive: pick "Z.AI Coding Plan".
266: opencode auth login          # → provider zai-coding-plan; model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2
267: ```
268: 
269: > Do not mix region endpoints (international `minimax.io` vs China `minimaxi.com`). On OpenCode 2, confirm live LLM Gateway slugs with `opencode models --standalone` filtered for `llmgateway/` (OpenCode 2 lists no minimax provider). On the OpenCode 1 fallback, confirm live model ids with `opencode models minimax-coding-plan` and live LLM Gateway slugs with `opencode models llmgateway`.
270: 
271: **On auth-error mid-dispatch** (`401 Unauthorized`, `provider/model not found`): invalidate the cache, rerun the pre-flight, and apply the same decision tree before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.
272: 
273: ### User-facing prompt templates
274: 
275: Surface these verbatim to the operator when the pre-flight decision tree lands on "ASK user" (default missing with a fallback configured, or all providers missing). Never dispatch until the operator responds.
276: 
277: **Default missing, fallback configured:**
278: 
279: ```text
280: The skill default is not configured on this machine (`llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on both OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2).
281: A configured fallback is available. Pick one:
282:   A) Use `-m openai/gpt-6-sol#high` on OpenCode 2 or `openai/gpt-6-sol --variant high` on the OpenCode 1 fallback (OpenAI flagship persona, configured now, paid)
283:   B) Use `kimi-for-coding/k2p7` (Kimi For Coding plan, configured now — subscription)
284:   C) Run the default provider's login first (`opencode providers login llmgateway` on OpenCode 2, `opencode providers login llmgateway` on the OpenCode 1 fallback), then retry the original dispatch
285:   D) Name a different model — paste the `--model <provider/model>` you want to use
286: ```
287: 
288: **All providers missing:**
289: 
290: ```text
291: No supported providers are configured on this machine. Run one:
292:   - `opencode providers login opencode-go`  (optional on OpenCode 1 — selectable Go gateway; fronts deepseek-v4.1-flash)
293:   - `opencode auth login`                   (MiniMax Token Plan — default MiniMax path; pick "MiniMax Token Plan (minimax.io)" → provider minimax-coding-plan; model minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3)
294:   - `opencode providers login minimax`      (MiniMax Direct API — pay-per-token; needs MINIMAX_API_KEY; model minimax/MiniMax-M3)
295:   - `opencode auth login`                   (LLM Gateway — pick "DevPass (LLM Gateway)" → provider llmgateway; the default route on both versions, model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017)
296:   - `opencode auth login`                   (Kimi For Coding plan — Kimi/Moonshot coding subscription; provider kimi-for-coding; model kimi-for-coding/k2p7)
297:   - `opencode auth login`                   (Z.AI GLM Coding Plan — GLM coding subscription; provider zai-coding-plan; model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2)
298:   - `opencode providers login openai`       (OpenAI premium alternative — paid)
299: Which would you like to set up? Confirm when login finishes; the skill will retry the original dispatch.
300: ```
301: 
302: **Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch returns an auth error after pre-flight passed (credential expired or rotated), invalidate the cache, rerun the pre-flight, and apply the same decision tree before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.
303: 
304: ---
305: 
306: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
307: 
308: On OpenCode 2 the default is `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max` (DevPass LLM Gateway, with flash max-tier-pinned by policy), once `opencode models --standalone` lists the `llmgateway/` prefix. On OpenCode 1 the default is the same model as `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max`, with reasoning effort expressed through `--variant`, which maps to a provider-specific effort scale. The model string is always `provider/model-id`. On OpenCode 2, list with `opencode models --standalone` and filter for the `<provider>/` prefix; `opencode models <provider>` lists the live options on OpenCode 1.
309: 
310: **Full provider/model roster, the GPT-6 slug grid and the per-provider effort map (`--variant` levels on OpenCode 1, `-m provider/model#<level>` on OpenCode 2) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
311: 
312: ---
313: 
314: ## 6. AGENT FLAG
315: 
316: `--agent <slug>` loads an agent definition from `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. The agent definition's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, and system prompt that shape the dispatch.
317: 
318: ### Discovering agents
319: 
320: | Command | What it shows |
321: |---------|---------------|
322: | `opencode agent list` | All registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
323: | `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
324: | `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Skill resolution for a slug if the agent loads one |
325: 
326: ### Agent slugs in this repo
327: 
328: | Slug | Role |
329: |------|------|
330: | `general` | Implementation, default subagent |
331: | `context` | Read-only retrieval and search |
332: | `orchestrate` | Multi-agent coordination |
333: | `write` | Documentation generation |
334: | `review` | Code review and PR analysis |
335: | `debug` | Fresh-perspective debugging |
336: | `deep-research` | Iterative research loop executor |
337: | `deep-review` | Iterative code review loop executor |
338: | `ai-council` | Multi-strategy planning |
339: 
340: The cli-opencode skill defers to the calling AI on agent selection. See `references/agent-delegation.md` for the routing matrix and `assets/prompt-templates.md` for canonical invocation shapes.
341: 
342: ---
343: 
344: ## 7. OUTPUT FORMAT AND EVENT STREAM
345: 
346: `--format default` produces a human-formatted log. `--format json` emits a newline-delimited JSON event stream.
347: 
348: ### JSON event shape (OpenCode 2.0.32 and OpenCode 1.19.3)
349: 
350: Each line is a JSON object with at minimum:
351: 
352: | Field | Meaning |
353: |-------|---------|
354: | `type` | Event type (`step_start`, `tool_use`, `text`, `step_finish`) |
355: | `timestamp` | Unix time in milliseconds, as a number |
356: | `sessionID` | The session id assigned by OpenCode |
357: | `part` | Type-specific payload |
358: 
359: External runtimes parse the stream incrementally to surface tool calls, partial messages and the final summary. cli-opencode prompt templates always pass `--format json` so the calling AI parses structured events instead of guessing format boundaries. The two versions emit the same event names.
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 8. STATE LOCATION AND SHARE URLS
364: 
365: ### State directory
366: 
367: OpenCode persists session state in a shared SQLite database and storage tree under `~/.local/share/opencode/`:
368: 
369: - `opencode.db` (`-shm`/`-wal` companions): the session/message database
370: - `storage/`: per-session structured artifacts
371: - `snapshot/`: working-tree snapshots
372: 
373: There is no per-session directory under `~/.opencode/state/<sessionID>/` on a standard install, so that path does not exist on this runtime layout. To inspect a specific session, use `opencode export <sessionID>` (§3) rather than reading files from a state directory. The cli-opencode self-invocation guard's Layer 3 lock-file probe (`~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock`, per ADR-001) targets the older path as a best-effort third layer on top of the env-var and process-ancestry checks. Treat it as a heuristic, not a verified-present artifact, on installs where `~/.opencode/state/` does not exist.
374: 
375: ### Share URLs
376: 
377: On OpenCode 2 `run` there is no `--share` flag at all. On the OpenCode 1 fallback (1.19.3), `--share` is a hidden, deprecated option: it prints `!  Session sharing has been discontinued`, publishes nothing and prints no URL. No dispatch passes it and there is no share URL to publish.
378: 
379: ---
380: 
381: ## 9. VERSION DRIFT
382: 
383: This reference is pinned to OpenCode 2 at 2.1.4, the recommended target, and OpenCode 1 at 1.19.4, the fallback for users who have not updated. If the live binary reports a different version, do the following:
384: 
385: 1. Run `opencode run --help` and diff the flag list against Section 4.
386: 2. Run `opencode --help` and diff the subcommand list against Section 3.
387: 3. If a flag was renamed, prefer the new name in the dispatch. If a flag was removed, fall back to the closest analogue and surface the drift in the calling AI's response.
388: 4. If the operator's machine has a major version bump (v1.4+, v2.x), re-validate the entire skill against the new flag table and bump the cli-opencode minor version.
389: 
390: ### Failure modes specific to drift
391: 
392: | Symptom | Likely cause |
393: |---------|--------------|
394: | `unknown option --variant` (OpenCode 1 only) | v1.2 or earlier, when the variant flag was named `--reasoning`. On OpenCode 2 the effort rides on the model id instead (`-m provider/model#<level>`) |
395: | `"!  Session sharing has been discontinued" on stderr (OpenCode 1 only)` | `--share` was passed; on 1.19.3 it is a deprecated no-op. Drop the flag. OpenCode 2 `run` has no `--share` |
396: | `unknown option --format json` | v1.0, when the JSON event stream was the default and the flag did not exist |
397: | `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | Plugin loader crash, so rerun with `--pure` (OpenCode 1 only) to bypass plugins |
398: 
399: ---
400: 
401: ## 10. TROUBLESHOOTING
402: 
403: | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
404: |---------|-------|-----|
405: | `command not found: opencode` | Binary not on PATH | Install via standalone installer or `brew install opencode` |
406: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD required` | Server enforces basic auth | Pass `-p <password>` or set the env var |
407: | `provider/model not found` | Provider not configured | Run `opencode providers` to enumerate, then `auth login <provider>` |
408: | Empty output stream | `--format default` with non-TTY parent | Pass `--format json` and parse the event stream |
409: | Session never finishes | Tool call hung | Run `opencode export <sessionID>` and inspect the message log it returns |
410: | Plugin load crash | Misconfigured plugin | Rerun with `--pure` (OpenCode 1 only) to bypass all plugins |
411: | Self-invocation refused | cli-opencode detected an in-OpenCode runtime | Use a sibling cli-* skill or a fresh shell session. See ADR-001 |
412: | `--share` passed (OpenCode 1 only) | Nothing is published on 1.19.3, the flag only prints a warning | Drop the flag |
413: 
414: ---
415: 
416: ## 11. RELATED RESOURCES
417: 
418: - `./integration-patterns.md` - The three documented use cases and their copy-paste invocation shapes
419: - `./agent-delegation.md` - Agent routing matrix and invocation patterns
420: - `./opencode-tools.md` - Unique capabilities (full plugin/skill/MCP runtime, parallel detached sessions)
421: - `../assets/prompt-templates.md` - Copy-paste prompt templates per use case
422: - `../assets/prompt-quality-card.md` - Framework selection and CLEAR 5-check
423: - `../SKILL.md` - Skill entry point and routing summary
424: - `../ROUTER.md` §3 - Machine router: intent map, resource map and loading levels

15: 
16: # OpenCode CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for the OpenCode CLI binary, every subcommand the cli-opencode skill dispatches against, the flag set it relies on, the agent surface it can target and the failure modes that need explicit handling. Version baselines: OpenCode 2 at 2.1.4, the recommended target, and OpenCode 1 at 1.19.4, the backwards-compatible fallback for users who have not updated.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: OpenCode is the framework that owns this repository. The same binary that hosts the operator's TUI session also accepts non-interactive invocations through `opencode run`. The cli-opencode skill calls `opencode run` from external runtimes (Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell) so the calling AI can dispatch a task into a fresh OpenCode session that loads the full plugin, skill, and MCP runtime.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Provide a single-source reference for the OpenCode CLI surface: every subcommand cli-opencode invokes, every flag it pins, every agent it can route to, the version baselines it is built against and the error envelopes that need explicit recovery.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Looking up an OpenCode CLI subcommand or flag during a delegation
35: - Selecting a model + variant + agent for a dispatch
36: - Confirming the version baseline before pinning a flag set
37: - Troubleshooting a failed `opencode run` invocation
38: - Confirming the self-invocation guard signal against the live binary
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Binary** | `opencode` for OpenCode 2, the recommended target; side by side, the OpenCode 1 fallback is `opencode1`, and a v1-only machine names it `opencode`. With no `OPENCODE_BIN`, resolution takes the first `opencode2` anywhere on `PATH` and only falls back to the first `opencode` in `PATH` order when none exists |
45: | **Repository** | https://github.com/sst/opencode |
46: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 2 (recommended): 2.1.4 |
47: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 1 (fallback): 1.19.4 |
48: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ for the npm install path or the standalone binary on macOS |
49: 
50: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. INSTALLATION
55: 
56: | Method | Command | Notes |
57: |--------|---------|-------|
58: | **Standalone** | `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash` | macOS / Linux installer |
59: | **Homebrew** | `brew install opencode` | macOS package manager |
60: | **npm global** | `npm install -g opencode-ai` | Cross-platform when Node.js 18+ is present |
61: | **Upgrade** | `opencode upgrade [target]` | Pin a specific version with the `target` argument |
62: | **Uninstall** | `opencode uninstall` | Removes the binary and related state |
63: 
64: After installation, run `opencode --version` to confirm. The cli-opencode skill is pinned to two baselines: OpenCode 2 at 2.1.4, the recommended target, and OpenCode 1 at 1.19.4, the fallback for users who have not updated. Newer binaries may add or rename flags, so consult Section 9 (Version Drift) before relying on a non-pinned flag.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 3. SUBCOMMAND MAP
69:

73: |------------|---------|-------------------------|
74: | `opencode` (default) | Start the TUI in the current project | No (interactive only) |
75: | `opencode run [message..]` | Non-interactive single-shot dispatch | YES (canonical use case) |

81: | `opencode debug` | Debugging and troubleshooting tools | YES (for `debug skill` and `debug agent` listings) |
